::: {.why}
The standard fix for a unit root removes the level information, and for a spread that is exactly the information the trade lives on, which is the gap week 12 fills.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Say what differencing does to a series' long-run relationship, and give one example where the differenced series is useless for the decision you need to make.
- State the practical consequence of a near-unit-root series being differenced when it should not have been.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Demonstrate the loss: take your mean-reverting spread, difference it, and try to build a trading rule from the differenced series alone. Then build the same rule from the level. Report both Sharpe ratios. The differenced version cannot see the level, so it cannot know when the spread is wide.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Read the section of the Forecasting: Principles and Practice ARIMA chapter on differencing and over-differencing, and write down the ACF signature of an over-differenced series so that you can recognise it later.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the setup for next week in one paragraph: two series that are individually non-stationary, whose difference is stationary, is a structure that neither differencing nor levels regression handles correctly.
:::
:::
